chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Kahmas, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered the bathhouse and I wanted to exit from it, so he said: 'O Muhammad! Did you not get waxing done?' So I said: 'I did apply with it a few days ago'. So he said: 'But do you not know that it is a cleansing?'

key_terms.تَطَّلِي: to get waxed / to remove hair with wax

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hair removal (waxing) in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages the narrator to remove hair wax (tatheel) from his body, explicitly defining the act as *tahoor* (purification). This establishes a foundational Shia legal principle that physical grooming is not merely aesthetic but an integral component of ritual purity (*taharah*), reflecting the holistic view of cleanliness in Islamic jurisprudence. The narration highlights the Imam's attention to daily practices, linking bodily care directly to spiritual and ritual readiness.
